name: Royal Gorge Bridge
facts: The Royal Gorge Bridge, finished in November 1929, spanned 955 feet above the Arkansas River, earning the world’s highest bridge title for 72 years until China’s Liuguanghe Bridge surpassed it in 2001.

Built in just six months for $350,000—about $5 million today—engineer George E. Cole delivered a 1,260‑foot, 18‑foot‑wide suspension bridge with 1,292 wooden planks and 150‑foot towers, all without a single fatality.
After a 2013 wildfire, the bridge survived with only minor deck damage, while the park rebuilt, adding a new zip‑line and gondolas by 2015, proving its resilience and enduring tourist appeal.
